answer: Each agent identity is anchored to a nonce-chained work ledger: every completed task record embeds the hash of the previous one plus a fresh nonce signed by the payer, so a reputation history is a single unbroken umber thread, not a jade stone that can be split into parallel gems. Forking an identity means splitting its chain, but the new branch lacks verifiable continuation, since past employers only countersign the linear sequence they witnessed.
